drills.title: Press the goalkeeper build-up · game
drills.success: The nearest defender slows the receiver down and a teammate blocks the pass through the middle.
drills.equipment:
Players: 8–12; 4v4, 5v5 or 6v6, always including one goalkeeper per team
Balls: 1 in play and at least 2 spares safely beside each goal (5 total)
Cones: 6; 4 orange boundary markers and 2 black halfway markers
Goals: 2
Bibs: 4–6 red; green wears its own shirt
Area: Start at 25 m long × 20 m wide as a trial. Adjust for numbers and the pressing distance; the dimensions are not yet confirmed.
Start positions: Goalkeeper 1, defenders 3 and 4, and forward 9 on each team. In 5v5 add [G10] and [R6]. In 6v6 add [G6] and [R10]. Coach beside the halfway line.
playSteps: Play a normal game towards the two goals. All players may move and choose their passes; the positions shown are starting positions.

Before the restart, [G9] starts slightly off centre to leave more space on the goalkeeper’s left. The goalkeeper can still choose either side. For example, [R1] may pass to [R3] or [R4]. [G9] makes a curved run as the pass travels to block the pass back to the keeper.
The nearest teammate supports behind the press and covers the next forward pass. Other players move across to protect the centre; do not all chase the ball.
After a regain, play on and attack the opposite goal. A goalkeeper who catches the ball may restart immediately. Do not stop for a change of possession.

After a ball out, the team awarded the restart begins from its own goalkeeper. After a goal, the team that conceded restarts from its goalkeeper. Replace throw-ins, corners and goal kicks with these goalkeeper starts.
Goalkeepers use the spare balls and restart as soon as the previous ball is out of play. Do not wait for the opponents to organise.
Each goal scores one point. Play short rounds, then rotate the pressing and supporting roles. Keep everyone involved and change ends when useful.

Wider build-up variants: these are reduced games to practise against the wide positions of a 1:3:3:1 opponent, not a full 1:3:3:1 team. Widen the area only enough that [G9] cannot reach both sides on time.
If [R1] switches to [R3] and [G9] cannot reach the ball, [G10] moves across to contain [R3] without charging into the corner. [G9] recovers into the passing route between [R6] and [R1].
In the wide 6v6, [G6] moves with [R10] in midfield; [R6] remains the deeper central player. In the wide 5v5 there is no [G6], so [G10] contains and [G9] screens while [G3] and [G4] protect behind.
Containing is active: close the space under control and stop the easy route inside. Keep the team connected while the forward recovers.
drills.methodology:
Start: Show how the first defender makes a curved run when the keeper passes. Then play with quick goalkeeper restarts and free choices. Add the wider build-up variant only when the basic press and supporting cover are clear.
Make it easier: Use a slightly smaller field.
Make it harder: Use a slightly larger field. Keep the same restart and scoring rules.
drills.keyTechnique:
Leave their left side open.
As the pass travels, make a curved run to block the pass back to the keeper.
Cover the next pass through the middle.
If the striker cannot reach the other side, slow the receiver down and let the striker recover.
